task: Carry the box to the exit, and whenever the box falls, pick it up again.

calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task says 'Carry the box to the exit', which requires the box to be in the agent's hands when it reaches the exit, but no clause ties holding_box to at_exit. Existence(at_exit) alone lets the agent pick the box up after a fall, drop it (the environment allows 'drop the box onto an empty cell in front once the first fall has happened'), and walk out empty-handed. The machine transition (u0, at_exit&!box_fell) -> u2 pays 11 without checking holding_box. Add a hard Response(at_exit, holding_box), the same pattern as 'carry c to g': at_exit is true only on the last step, so the box must be held on that step. Keep Existence(at_exit) and Response(box_fell, holding_box); both are correct.

calls.candidate: hard Existence(at_exit), hard Response(at_exit, holding_box), hard Response(box_fell, holding_box)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(at_exit) is the hard goal of reaching the exit. Response(at_exit, holding_box) is the carry-to-exit requirement, so the box must be in hand on the exit step. Response(box_fell, holding_box) is the whenever-falls-pick-it-up-again rule, owed after each fall and met by any later pickup. All three clauses are hard, none is redundant, no requirement is added beyond the task, and the machine pays only when the box is held at the exit.
